s: What was the status of the Kartarpur Corridor after Operation Sindoor in May 2025?
o: It was transferred to the United Nations.
It was declared a non-binding protocol.
x: The Kartarpur Corridor, which had opened in 2019, was suspended after Operation Sindoor in May 2025. The 2019 opening is its earlier status, not the post-Operation Sindoor development.

s: Operation Sindoor was India's response to the terror attack on tourists at which place?
x: Operation Sindoor followed the Pahalgam terror attack and involved overt military action against Pakistan-based terror infrastructure.

s: Who led the Operation Sindoor outreach delegation (May 2025) that included AP MP Daggubati Purandeswari?
x: Purandeswari was in Ravi Shankar Prasad's delegation; Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu went with Supriya Sule and GM Harish Balayogi with Shashi Tharoor.

s: Under Operation Sindoor (6-7 May 2025), how many terror camps in Pakistan and PoK did India strike?
x: Operation Sindoor struck nine terror camps after the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025.

s: For which occasion were Sikh jathas denied permission to visit Nankana Sahib in November 2025?
o: The opening anniversary of the Kartarpur Corridor
x: The denied Sikh jathas were intended to visit Nankana Sahib for Guru Nanak's birth anniversary in November 2025. Maharaja Ranjit Singh's death anniversary was a separate occasion linked to the earlier denial in June 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India–Pakistan religious-visit framework?
o: Nankana Sahib, in Pakistan's Punjab, is the birthplace of Guru Nanak
The Simla Agreement of 1972 has a non-binding exchanges clause
The 1974 Protocol covers Nankana Sahib and Ajmer Sharif
x: Katas Raj is in Punjab; it is Shadani Darbar that is in Sindh.

s: Who were the two US officials associated with the May 2025 India–Pakistan ceasefire announcement?
o: Vice President Marco Rubio and Secretary of State J.D. Vance
Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio
Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Donald Trump
Vice President Marco Rubio and Secretary of State Donald Trump
x: The US officials were Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The other options incorrectly interchange the offices or include Donald Trump instead of one of the two officials identified.

s: Who is Pakistan's army chief referred to in the discussion of India's diplomatic challenges?
x: Pakistan's army chief is Field Marshal Asim Munir.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the regional fallout of Operation Sindoor?
o: India treats Kashmir as a bilateral matter
The ceasefire was announced by US President Donald Trump
China reportedly backed India, creating a two-front threat for Pakistan
Pakistan's army chief is Field Marshal Asim Munir
x: China reportedly backed Pakistan, raising a two-front threat for India, not the reverse.

s: From 21 May 2025, how many multi-party delegations did India send abroad on cross-border terrorism after Operation Sindoor?
x: Seven multi-party delegations went to world capitals from 21 May 2025.

s: Nankana Sahib, to which India denied Sikh jathas in November 2025, is the birthplace of whom?
x: Nankana Sahib in Pakistan's Punjab is the birthplace of Guru Nanak (1469).

s: Which AP MP was part of the Operation Sindoor outreach delegation led by Shashi Tharoor to the USA, Panama, Guyana, Brazil and Colombia?
x: GM Harish Balayogi (TDP, Amalapuram) was in Shashi Tharoor's delegation to the Americas.

s: In which year was the Kartarpur Corridor opened?
x: The Kartarpur Corridor opened in 2019 and was suspended after Operation Sindoor in May 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the JCPOA and Iran's nuclear programme?
o: Germany was a party to the JCPOA
The United States withdrew from the JCPOA in 2019
Israel–US strikes hit Iranian nuclear sites in June 2025
x: The United States withdrew from the JCPOA in 2018, not 2019.

s: Which set of Iranian nuclear-related sites was targeted when the United States joined the Israel–Iran conflict in June 2025?
x: The targeted sites were Natanz, Fordow and Isfahan. Al-Udeid was later targeted by Iran in retaliation, while Qom and Tehran were not listed among the three sites struck by the United States.

s: The GBU-57 MOP used in the June 2025 strikes is best described as which of the following?
x: The GBU-57 MOP is a 30,000-pound conventional bunker buster. The solid-fuel missile was the Kheybar Shekan, while Tomahawk was a separate weapon.

s: Which country is not an NPT signatory and has no IAEA inspections of its undeclared nuclear arsenal?
x: Israel is not an NPT signatory and has no IAEA inspections; Iran was only debating an NPT-exit bill in June 2025.

s: Which Iranian site, struck in June 2025, was Iran's main uranium enrichment centre?
x: Natanz was the main enrichment centre; Fordow was the underground facility under a mountain near Qom.

s: In which country is the US Al-Udeid Air Base, struck by Iran in June 2025?
x: Iran struck Al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar with advance notice; the ceasefire was announced by Trump.

s: Which Article of the UN Charter bars the use of force?
x: Article 2 of the UN Charter bars the use of force.

s: At what level do the UN snapback sanctions reimposed on Iran in 2025 ban uranium enrichment?
x: The snapback measures include a ban on enrichment at any level, besides asset freezes, travel bans and an arms embargo.

s: Who described the UNSC snapback sanctions reimposed on Iran as “unjust and illegal” and recalled envoys from France, Germany and the UK?
x: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called the sanctions “unjust and illegal” and recalled envoys from France, Germany and the UK. Bezalel Smotrich was identified in connection with opposition to the Gaza peace plan, not Iran’s response to the sanctions.

s: How did Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi describe the US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites?
o: A historic achievement for regional security
A lawful act under the NPT
A grave violation of the UN Charter and NPT
x: Abbas Araghchi called the strikes a “grave violation” of the UN Charter and the NPT. “Historic” was the description attributed to Israel’s Prime Minister Netanyahu.

s: Which of the following Iranian proxy group–country pairs is correctly matched?
x: Hezbollah is linked to Lebanon; the Houthis are in Yemen and Hashd al-Shaabi in Iraq.

s: Which of the following countries was a party to the 2015 JCPOA with Iran as part of the P5+1?
x: The P5+1 was the US, UK, France, Russia, China and Germany.

s: Which Iranian nuclear site, struck by the US in June 2025, lies under a mountain near Qom?
x: Fordow is the underground site near Qom, hit by GBU-57 bunker busters from B-2 bombers; Natanz is the main enrichment site.

s: Who became the leader of Hezbollah after Hassan Nasrallah was killed in 2024?
x: Naim Qassem now leads Hezbollah (Lebanon) after Nasrallah was killed in 2024.

s: Kheybar Shekan, a solid-fuel missile used in the June 2025 conflict, belongs to which country?
x: Kheybar Shekan is Iran's solid-fuel missile used in its retaliation during the 12-day war.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Iran signed the NPT in 1968 and ratified it in 1970.
2. Israel is a signatory of the NPT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Iran signed the NPT in 1968 and ratified it in 1970; Israel is not an NPT signatory.

s: How many hostages were taken and people killed in the Hamas attack on Israel of 7 October 2023?
x: The 7 October 2023 attack involved 251 hostages and 1,219 people killed.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gaza ceasefire:
1. Hamas agreed to disarm as part of the ceasefire arrangements.
2. The Israeli withdrawal remained incomplete.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Hamas refused to disarm, so 1 is wrong; the incomplete Israeli withdrawal was one of the challenges facing the ceasefire.

s: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi was sworn in again as President in 2024 of which country?
x: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi won a third term as President of Egypt in December 2023 with 89.6% of the vote and was sworn in again in 2024.

s: Which of the following is true of the US executive order 'Assuring the Security of the State of Qatar', unlike a treaty?
o: can be repealed by a future president
is legally binding on future presidents
x: As an executive order and not a treaty, it needed no Senate approval and can be repealed by a future president.

s: Where was the Gaza Declaration ceasefire of 13 October 2025 signed by Donald Trump and the guarantor countries?
x: The Gaza Declaration was signed at Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, with Egypt, Qatar and Turkiye as guarantors; Doha hosted the Afghanistan–Pakistan ceasefire.

s: What triggered the US executive order 'Assuring the Security of the State of Qatar'?
o: Iran's missile strike on the Al-Udeid base
Israeli airstrikes in Qatar targeting Hamas leaders
The reimposition of UNSC snapback sanctions on Iran
x: The order followed Israeli airstrikes in Qatar targeting Hamas leaders about three weeks earlier, which Qatar called “state terror”.

s: Which provision did the language of the US executive order 'Assuring the Security of the State of Qatar' mirror?
x: The order's language mirrored NATO Article 5; it was part of Trump's 20-point Gaza plan.

s: During the Sharm el-Sheikh ceasefire diplomacy, whom did Donald Trump praise and with whom did he meet?
o: He praised Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and met Mahmoud Abbas
He praised Mahmoud Abbas and met Abdel Fattah El-Sisi
He praised the Emir of Qatar and met the Turkish President
He praised Benjamin Netanyahu and met the Egyptian Defence Minister
x: Donald Trump praised Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and met Mahmoud Abbas. The other combinations change the individuals involved in these two engagements.

s: Since which year has Qatar been a Major Non-NATO Ally of the United States?
x: Qatar has been an MNNA since 2022 and hosts Al-Udeid, the largest US base in the Middle East.

s: Which is the largest US military base in the Middle East?
x: Al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar is the largest US base in the Middle East and the heart of CENTCOM operations.

s: What was the significance of Amir Khan Muttaqi’s visit to India during 9–16 October 2025?
o: It marked the beginning of the Moscow Dialogue in 2017.
It was the first official visit by a top Taliban leader to India since the Taliban returned to power in 2021.
It resulted in the reopening of India’s technical mission in Kabul in June 2022.
It was the first meeting between an Indian Ambassador and the Taliban in Doha in August 2021.
x: Amir Khan Muttaqi’s visit was the first official visit by a top Taliban leader to India since the Taliban returned to power in 2021. The Moscow Dialogue was held in 2017, while the technical mission was reopened in June 2022 and an Indian Ambassador met the Taliban in Doha in August 2021.

s: To what was India's technical mission in Kabul upgraded after the Jaishankar–Muttaqi meeting in 2025?
o: a full embassy headed by a Charge d'Affaires
a full embassy headed by an Ambassador
x: The mission became a full embassy headed by a Charge d'Affaires; India still does not formally recognise the Taliban.

s: Which of the following is an Indian project in Afghanistan?
x: The Zaranj–Delaram Highway and the Salma Dam are separate Indian projects in Afghanistan.

s: Whom did India back during 1996–2001, when it had no ties with the Taliban?
x: In 1996–2001 India backed the Northern Alliance; it still does not formally recognise the Taliban regime.

s: What is the full form of PTM in the Afghanistan–Pakistan context?
x: PTM is the Pashtun Tahafuz Movement; TTP is Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan.

s: The immediate ceasefire agreed in Doha on 19 October 2025 between Afghanistan and Pakistan was mediated by which countries?
x: The Doha ceasefire was mediated by Qatar and Turkiye, with both Defence Ministers attending. Saudi Arabia supported the ceasefire but was not identified as a mediator.

s: What was reported during Muttaqi’s visit to India in the Afghanistan–Pakistan border clashes along the Durand Line?
o: India deployed forces on both sides of the Durand Line
Afghanistan carried out airstrikes in Pakistan, while Pakistani forces captured Afghan posts
Both countries agreed to withdraw from the Durand Line
Pakistan carried out airstrikes in Afghanistan, while Afghan forces captured Pakistani posts
x: Pakistan carried out airstrikes in Afghanistan, and Afghan forces captured posts during the clashes. The other options reverse the actions or introduce developments not associated with this episode.

s: The Durand Line, which divides Pashtun-populated areas, was demarcated in which year?
x: The Durand Line was drawn by the British in 1893. It divides the Pashtuns and has never been recognised by Afghanistan.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Doha ceasefire of 19 October 2025?
o: The threat groups identified included IS-K and al-Qaida affiliates
Afghanistan announced a boycott of the cricket series
Pakistani airstrikes in Paktika targeted the Hafiz Gul Bahadur group
Follow-up talks were scheduled in Kabul
x: Follow-up talks were to take place in Doha, not Kabul.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Durand Line:
1. It was drawn by the British in 1893.
2. It has been formally recognised by Afghanistan.
3. It is about 2,611 km long.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; Afghanistan has never recognised the Durand Line.

s: How much has India invested in development in Afghanistan since 2001?
x: India has invested over USD 3 billion in Afghanistan's development since 2001.

s: Through which port has India's trade with Afghanistan been routed?
x: India's trade with Afghanistan goes via Chabahar in Iran, avoiding Pakistan.

s: What is the full form of TTP in the Afghanistan–Pakistan context?
x: TTP stands for Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan.

s: Near which place did Nepal's Gen Z protest of 8 September 2025 begin?
o: The Mandala monument at Maitighar, Kathmandu
x: The protest began near the Mandala monument at Maitighar in Kathmandu before the Parliament complex was stormed.

s:
Assertion (A): The social media ban in Nepal was revoked after the Gen Z protests.
Reason (R): The probe panel was required to report within 30 days.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is true because the outcome included revocation of the social media ban. Reason R is false: the probe panel was to report in 15 days, not 30 days.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recent democratic crises in South Asia?
o: Sri Lanka's 2022 Aragalaya was directed against Gotabaya Rajapaksa
Bangladesh's 2024 July Uprising was directed against Sheikh Hasina
Nepal's 2025 Gen Z protest against K.P. Sharma Oli followed a social media ban
x: The Bangladesh July Uprising lasted 21 days, not 30.

s: Who led the government of Bangladesh during the reported US military activity in Chittagong?
x: Bangladesh's government at the time was led by Muhammad Yunus.

s: India and China agreed to resume border trade through which pass, leading to an objection from Nepal?
x: The proposed resumption of India–China border trade was through Lipulekh Pass in Uttarakhand. Kalapani and Limpiyadhura were part of Nepal's territorial claim, not the pass named for the trade route.

s: Which of the following statements regarding US military activity in Chittagong, Bangladesh, is incorrect?
o: A US C-130J Super Hercules landed at Shah Amanat International Airport.
The aircraft is usually based at Yokota Airbase, Japan.
The activities included Operation Pacific Angel-25 and Tiger Lightning-2025.
The activity established a permanent US military base in Chittagong.
x: The incorrect statement is that a permanent US military base was established in Chittagong; there was no permanent US base. The aircraft landed at Shah Amanat International Airport, and the activities included Operation Pacific Angel-25 and Tiger Lightning-2025.

s: In the context of Nepal's Gen Z protests, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: “Nepo babies” – Organisation that coordinated the protests
Hami Nepal – Slogan targeted by the protesters
K.P. Sharma Oli – Home Minister who resigned
Ramesh Lekhak – Home Minister who resigned
x: Ramesh Lekhak was the Home Minister who resigned; Hami Nepal coordinated the protests, “nepo babies” was a slogan and Oli was the Prime Minister who resigned.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's response to Nepal's objection to Lipulekh trade?
o: India said the objection was fully based on historical facts.
It was given by MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.
The trade was to resume through Lipulekh Pass in Uttarakhand.
x: India said Nepal's objection was NOT based on historical facts and was unilateral.

s: On which side of the Mahakali River does Nepal's constitutional map place Kalapani, Limpiyadhura and Lipulekh?
x: Nepal's map places the three areas east of the Mahakali River.

s: Whose government fell as a result of the Gen Z protests of September 2025 in Nepal?
x: The protests toppled the government of K.P. Sharma Oli in Nepal.

s: What is the total cost of the two India–Bhutan cross-border railway projects (Kokrajhar–Gelephu and Banarhat–Samtse)?
x: The two projects together cost ₹4,033 crore; the Kokrajhar–Gelephu line is 69 km long with six stations.

s: How is the Bhutanese portion of the India–Bhutan cross-border railway projects funded?
o: Bhutan's 13th Five-Year Plan via the Ministry of External Affairs
Bhutan's 12th Five-Year Plan via the Ministry of Railways
x: The Bhutanese portion is funded through Bhutan's 13th Five-Year Plan via the MEA; Special Railway Projects fund the Indian portion.

s: In which year was the Sugauli Treaty, at the root of the India–Nepal Lipulekh dispute, concluded?
x: The Sugauli Treaty dates to 1815; the dispute is about the origin of the Mahakali River.

s: What is the approximate value of the China-backed Teesta River Comprehensive Management and Restoration Project, demanded by protesters in Bangladesh in October 2025?
x: Protesters in Chattogram and Rangpur demanded the $1 billion Chinese Teesta project.

s: Which UNCLOS Article calls for cooperation in semi-enclosed seas such as the Palk Bay and Gulf of Mannar?
x: UNCLOS Article 123 provides for cooperation among States bordering semi-enclosed seas.

s: Where is Tso Lhamo Lake, the source of the Teesta river?
x: The Teesta rises in Tso Lhamo Lake in Sikkim, not Bangladesh.

s: Which fisheries practice was banned by Sri Lanka in 2017 in the India–Sri Lanka fisheries dispute?
x: Sri Lanka banned bottom trawling in 2017. The other fishing practices listed were not identified as the practice banned in the stated context.

s: In which year was Katchatheevu, an uninhabited islet in the Palk Strait, placed under Sri Lanka by the India–Sri Lanka Maritime Boundary Treaty?
x: The 1974 Maritime Boundary Treaty placed Katchatheevu under Sri Lanka.

s: What is the length of the Kokrajhar–Gelephu cross-border rail line between India and Bhutan?
x: Kokrajhar–Gelephu is 69 km; Banarhat–Samtse is 20 km; both are fully funded by India.

s: What was India's share under the 2011 draft Teesta water-sharing arrangement?
x: The 2011 draft gave India 42.5% and Bangladesh 37.5%.

s: In which district of Uttarakhand is the Lipulekh Pass located?
x: Lipulekh Pass is in Pithoragarh district, at the India–Nepal–China (Tibet) tri-junction.

s: Since which year has India–China border trade been carried on through the Lipulekh Pass?
x: Trade via Lipulekh began in 1954; it was disrupted by COVID-19 and is now to resume.

s: What is the approximate width of the Siliguri Corridor at its narrowest?
x: The Siliguri Corridor ('Chicken's Neck') is only about 20–22 km wide.

s: The Banarhat–Samtse cross-border rail line links West Bengal with which country?
x: Banarhat (West Bengal)–Samtse (Bhutan) is a 20 km line fully funded by India.

s: TVS Motor announced an investment of how much in Solihull, UK, for Norton Motorcycles?
x: TVS Motor's Solihull investment was £250 million, not £100 million.

s: What is the European Union's number among India's FTA partners?
x: The EU is India's 22nd FTA partner.

s: At the 3rd India–EU Trade and Technology Council meeting, with which Indian platform was a pilot proposed to link the EU Digital Identity Wallet?
x: The pilot links DigiLocker, not Aadhaar, with the EU Digital Identity Wallet.

s: When was the comprehensive India–UK trade deal signed?
x: The deal was signed in July 2025; the FTA was still under implementation talks during Starmer's visit.

s: What was the US tariff on some Indian exports in 2025?
x: The US tariffs on some Indian exports were 50%, not 40%.

s: At what rate were pharmaceutical imports from the EU and Japan capped under the 2025 US pharmaceutical tariff?
x: The EU and Japan were capped at 15%; branded and patented imports otherwise faced 100%.

s: During UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's India visit, the £350 million missile deal was for which missile system and service?
o: STARStreak high velocity missiles for the Indian Navy
Lightweight Multirole Missiles for the Indian Army
ASRAAM for the Indian Air Force
Naval electric engines for India's Landing Platform Dock fleet
x: The £350 million deal concerned Lightweight Multirole Missiles made in Belfast for the Indian Army. STARStreak, ASRAAM and naval electric engines were separate defence-related developments.

s: Where was the 15th India–Japan Annual Summit (2025), attended by PM Modi and PM Shigeru Ishiba, held?
x: The 15th India–Japan Annual Summit was held in Tokyo.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the 15th India–Japan Annual Summit is incorrect?
o: Japan set a target of 10 trillion yen in private-sector investment in India over the next 10 years.
The summit produced 21 outcomes, including 13 agreements.
The India–Japan CEPA was terminated at the summit.
x: The incorrect statement is that the India–Japan CEPA was terminated; it was decided that the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement would be reviewed. The summit also involved a 10 trillion yen investment target, 21 outcomes including 13 agreements, and endorsement of Japan Industrial Townships.

s: Which of the following Indian State–Japanese prefecture partnerships is correctly matched?
x: The partnerships are Andhra Pradesh–Toyama, Tamil Nadu–Ehime, Uttar Pradesh–Yamanashi and Gujarat–Shizuoka.

s: Which was the first OECD member with which India signed a Bilateral Investment Treaty under its new investment treaty framework?
x: Israel was the first OECD member to sign a BIT with India under the new framework; the treaty has no tariff provisions.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the New Strategic EU–India Agenda?
o: The EU is India's second-largest trading partner
Multilateral engagement is one of its priorities
Defence and security is one of its priorities
It has five priorities including trade, technology and connectivity
x: The EU is India's largest trading partner, not the second-largest.

s: Since which year have India and Japan had a 'Special Strategic and Global Partnership'?
x: The Special Strategic and Global Partnership dates from 2014.

s: Which two connectivity initiatives were highlighted in the New Strategic EU–India Agenda?
o: Special Railway Projects and Horizon Europe
x: The agenda highlighted IMEC, the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor, and the Global Gateway. The other pairs combine unrelated initiatives, policies or cooperation mechanisms.

s: Under the 2025 India–Japan Annual Summit outcomes, how many Indians were to be trained in Japan?
x: The training target is 50,000 Indians; India runs a trade deficit with Japan.

s: Japan pledged to invest how much in India over the next decade?
x: Japan pledged ¥10 trillion over the next decade, in areas including infrastructure, manufacturing and clean energy.

s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Quad?
x: The Quad comprises India, Japan, Australia and the United States; China is not a member.

s: For which Indian naval fleet was Integrated Full Electric Propulsion planned under the UK–India defence cooperation, and by when?
o: India's next Landing Platform Dock fleet, by 2030
x: Integrated Full Electric Propulsion was planned for India's next Landing Platform Dock fleet by 2030. The other options alter both the type of fleet or the timeline.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the US tariff on pharmaceutical imports announced in 2025?
o: A 100% tariff applied to branded and patented drug imports from 1 October 2025.
A firm building a plant in the US could qualify for exemption.
Generic drug imports were also subjected to the 100% tariff.
The tariff targeted patented medicines rather than generics.
x: Generics were excluded; the 100% tariff applied to branded and patented drugs, with an exemption for firms building a US plant.

s: Under the New Strategic EU–India Agenda, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Security of Information Agreement – India's participation
Trade and Technology Council – Information-security talks
x: The European Legal Gateway is the EU–India mechanism for mobility. Horizon Europe is the EU research programme India is in talks to join, the Security of Information Agreement is still under talks, and the Trade and Technology Council deals with trade and technology.

s: What was the status of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) under the US pharmaceutical tariff measure?
x: The inclusion of APIs remained uncertain; PhRMA objected to the measure.

s: India and Japan agreed to revise the Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation of which year?
x: They agreed to revise the 2008 Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–Israel economic relations?
o: Annual India–Israel trade is about USD 40 billion
FTA talks are the next step after the BIT
The BIT was signed in New Delhi on 8 September 2025
Israel is the first OECD member to sign a BIT under India's new framework
x: Annual India–Israel trade is about USD 4 billion, not 40 billion.

s: Where is India's first ASRAAM assembly and testing facility under UK–India defence ties?
x: India's first ASRAAM assembly and testing facility is in Hyderabad.

s: What is India's position among the EU's Security and Defence Partnerships in Asia?
x: It is the EU's 3rd in Asia, after Japan and South Korea.

s: Which Shinkansen series is to be used for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail under India–Japan ties?
x: The 2025 summit outcomes named the E10 series Shinkansen for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad HSR.

s: With which Japanese prefecture is Andhra Pradesh partnered under the India–Japan State–prefecture ties?
x: Andhra Pradesh is paired with Toyama; Tamil Nadu with Ehime, UP with Yamanashi and Gujarat with Shizuoka.

s: At which India–EU Summit were the India–EU FTA negotiations concluded in January 2026?
x: The FTA talks were concluded at the 16th India–EU Summit in January 2026.

s: Which trade agreement was described as the 'mother of all deals' when talks concluded in January 2026?
x: The India–EU FTA was called the 'mother of all deals'; the EU became India's 22nd FTA partner.

s: Where was the India–Israel Bilateral Investment Treaty signed on 8 September 2025?
x: Nirmala Sitharaman and Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich signed the BIT in New Delhi.

s: About what share of the generic medicines used in the United States does India supply?
x: India supplies about 40% of US generics, which is why generics were kept out of the 100% pharma tariff.

s: Which of the following was included among the areas of cooperation under the India–Morocco Defence Cooperation MoU?
o: Co-development and co-production of drones and counter-drone systems
Joint development of civilian nuclear reactors
Establishment of a bilateral space station
x: The MoU covers co-development and co-production, including drones and counter-drone systems, along with several other defence areas. Nuclear reactors, a common currency and a joint space station were not listed as areas of cooperation.

s: Who co-chaired the inaugural Australia–India Defence Ministers' Dialogue held in Canberra?
x: Rajnath Singh and Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles co-chaired the dialogue in Canberra. Keir Starmer and Narendra Modi were associated with the India–UK engagement, not this Australia–India dialogue.

s: Along with an Agreement on Information Sharing, which pact was signed at the inaugural Australia–India Defence Ministers' Dialogue?
o: MoU on Submarine Search and Rescue Cooperation
x: The Dialogue produced an Agreement on Information Sharing and a separate MoU on Submarine Search and Rescue Cooperation.

s: What was the maritime-security outcome announced at the inaugural Australia–India Defence Ministers' Dialogue in Canberra?
o: Terms of Reference for Joint Staff Talks
MoU on Submarine Search and Rescue Cooperation
x: The maritime-security outcome was the Joint Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap. The other options refer to agreements signed at the dialogue rather than the roadmap outcome.

s: To which Australian submarine rescue exercise was India invited following the inaugural Australia–India Defence Ministers' Dialogue?
x: India was invited to Australia's submarine rescue exercise Black Carillon. Talisman Sabre, Austrahind and Puk Puk were mentioned as exercises, but the invitation specifically concerned Black Carillon.

s: Which description best captures Morocco’s geographical and economic significance in the context of India–Morocco relations?
o: It lies between the Pacific and Mediterranean and is a major petroleum supplier to India
It lies between the Atlantic and Mediterranean and is a major phosphate and fertilizer supplier to India
It lies between the Atlantic and Indian Ocean and is a major uranium supplier to India
It lies between the Arctic and Atlantic and is a major wheat supplier to India
x: Morocco is situated between the Atlantic and Mediterranean and is a major phosphate and fertilizer supplier to India. The alternative descriptions change Morocco’s geographical location or its principal supply significance.

s: In which year was the India–Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership established, whose five years the inaugural Defence Ministers' Dialogue marked?
x: The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates to 2020; the dialogue in Canberra (9 Oct 2025) marked five years.

s: In which city did Rajnath Singh announce a new Defence Wing at the Indian Embassy?
x: A Defence Wing at the Indian Embassy in Rabat was announced with the India–Morocco Defence MoU.

s: Which set of organisations was dismantled by the Trump administration in the context of polarisation in Western democracies?
o: MAGA, USAID and the Great Replacement
USAID, NPR and Voice of America
x: The Trump administration dismantled USAID, NPR and Voice of America. The other sets mix in unrelated bodies such as NATO, UNHCR or think tanks.

s: In which year did the Galwan clash between India and China take place?
x: Galwan occurred in 2020; the India–China détente came post-Tianjin in 2025.

s: Which position did S. Jaishankar express regarding India’s relations with the United States at the Aravalli Summit?
o: India should prioritise the Belt and Road Initiative over Neighbourhood First
India must align with a bloc at any cost and discontinue Neighbourhood First
India should replace Russian oil with products re-exported by India
Relations with the US cannot come at any cost, alongside energy security from Russian oil and Neighbourhood First

Urja Suraksha — Indian operation in Venezuela after earthquakes
Mahadev — EU maritime mission in the Red Sea

o: relief to Myanmar after an earthquake
evacuation of Indians from Iran and West Asia
relief to Sri Lanka after a cyclone

x: Southern Spear is a US operation in the Caribbean.

s: With which country is India's Operation Amistad associated?
x: Amistad = Venezuela; Brahma = Myanmar; Sagar Bandhu = Sri Lanka.

x: Gulf and West Asia energy and diaspora ties are the focus of Link West; Act East looks to ASEAN, Japan and South Korea.

No First Use and credible minimum deterrence

x: The term minilateralism is credited to Miles Kahler in 1992.

x: India's Act East meets Thailand's 'Act West'; India's own Gulf policy is Link West.

x: Raksha is the Defence Ministry's 10-year framework for defence diplomacy.

s: How many pillars does the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI), launched at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok in 2019, have?
x: The IPOI has 7 pillars.

x: The Quad is India, the US, Japan and Australia; it has no Quad-level 2+2, though bilateral 2+2s exist among all four.

o: Pax Silica – India joined in February 2024

s: Which of the following pairs (port – host country) is correctly matched?

s: In which year did India's IPGL sign a 10-year contract for Chabahar's Shahid Beheshti terminal?
x: IPGL signed the 10-year contract on 13 May 2024.

x: JIMEX is the India–Japan naval exercise, alongside Veer Guardian (air force) and Dharma Guardian (army).

x: Garuda is an India-France air-force exercise. Varuna is the India-France naval exercise, while Veer Guardian is conducted with Japan's air forces.

x: DOSTI is a trilateral coast guard exercise of India, Maldives and Sri Lanka. The other combinations include countries that are not DOSTI participants.

s: Which of the following was held along with MILAN 2026 at Visakhapatnam in February 2026?
x: MILAN 2026 was held with IFR 2026 and the IONS Conclave at Visakhapatnam; DOSTI-16 was not part of these events.

s: Where was the 13th edition of the multilateral naval exercise MILAN (February 2026) held?

x: The first MILAN was at Port Blair in 1995; the 13th was at Visakhapatnam in 2026.

x: MILAN 2024 was the 12th edition; MILAN 2026 was the 13th.

x: Garuda is the India–France air exercise; Varuna is naval.

x: The 2nd Veer Guardian was held at Jodhpur in September 2026.

o: India, Sri Lanka, Maldives and Bangladesh

x: Varuna is the India–France navy exercise; Garuda is the air force one.

x: MILAN 2026 at Visakhapatnam saw first-time ships from Germany, the Philippines and the UAE.

x: AFINDEX-2023 was held at the Foreign Training Node, Aundh, Pune, with 23 African nations.

s: Garuda Shakti is a Special Forces exercise between India and which country?

x: Samudra Shakti (Navy) and Garuda Shakti (Special Forces) are India's exercises with Indonesia.

x: Russia signed a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty with Iran in 2025 (asked before). India, Saudi Arabia and Egypt did not sign such a treaty with Russia in 2025.

s: Who was the chief guest at India's Republic Day celebrations in 2016?
x: French President Francois Hollande was the 2016 chief guest; Barack Obama was the chief guest in 2015.

s: Which cities are linked by the Maitree Express, restored in April 2008 after 43 years?
x: The Maitree Express links Kolkata and Dhaka; the Bandhan Express (2017) links Kolkata and Khulna.

x: India and Vietnam became Strategic Partners in 2007 and Comprehensive Strategic Partners in 2016.

s: Where was the 16th India–Japan Annual Summit held?
x: The latest (16th) India–Japan Annual Summit was held in New Delhi.

s: In which year did India and Vietnam establish a Strategic Partnership?
x: India–Vietnam ties became a Strategic Partnership in 2007 and a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2016.

s: Which cities are linked by the Bandhan Express, started in 2017?
x: Bandhan Express (2017) links Kolkata with Khulna; Maitree Express links Kolkata with Dhaka.

s: In which sector did the Union Cabinet approve a cooperation MoU between India and South Africa?
x: The India–South Africa MoU covers the disability sector: assistive technology and expertise exchange.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: STA-1 was obtained in 2018, not 2020. LEMOA, COMCASA and BECA correspond to 2016, 2018 and 2020 respectively.

s: In which year was the India–China Strategic Economic Dialogue set up?
x: Set up in 2010, the Dialogue held six rounds in 2011-2019 and was suspended after Galwan in 2020.

s: Where was the 10th Thailand–India Defence Dialogue (June 2026) held?
x: The 10th Thailand–India Defence Dialogue was held in Bangkok in June 2026.

x: The inaugural Defence Strategic Dialogue was with New Zealand; India has 2+2 formats with Japan, Australia and Brazil.

s: Which India–US foundational pact was signed in 2020?
x: The order is LEMOA (2016) → COMCASA (2018) → BECA (2020); STA-1 came in 2018.

s: In which year was India granted Strategic Trade Authorisation-1 (STA-1) status by the United States?
x: STA-1 came in 2018, not 2020.

s: How many rounds of the India–China Strategic Economic Dialogue were held (2011–2019) before it was suspended after Galwan?
x: The Dialogue, set up in 2010, held six rounds (2011–2019) and was suspended after Galwan (2020).

s: Which of the following pairs (partner – dialogue format) is correctly matched?
x: India and Brazil hold a 2+2 political-military dialogue; the Quad has no 2+2 and New Zealand's is a Defence Strategic Dialogue.

s: Why has India's heavy reliance on Russian defence platforms been criticised?
o: Limits diversification of India's defence suppliers
x: Dependence on Russian platforms is criticised because it limits diversification of India's defence procurement sources.

s: By which year does Mission Sudarshan Chakra aim to build a multi-layer defence shield?
x: The multi-layer shield is targeted by 2035, modelled on Israel's Iron Dome.

s: With which company is the engine for India's AMCA Mk-2 to be co-developed?
x: The AMCA Mk-2 engine is to be co-developed with Safran, while the GE F414 is meant for AMCA Mk-1.

s: Of which country's origin is the S-400 Triumf air-defence system, referred to as 'Sudarshan Chakra' in India?
x: The S-400 Triumf is a Russian-origin system with a stated range of 400 km.

s: In which year was the deal signed under which the Indian Air Force bought 36 Rafale jets?
x: The 36 IAF Rafales came under the 2016 deal, not 2019; the 114 MRFA jets got AoN in February 2026.

s: On whose technology are India's Kalvari-class (Scorpene) submarines based?
x: The Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines use French Naval Group technology and are built at MDL; Italy's WASS supplies their torpedoes.

s: With reference to BrahMos, which country is its first export customer, and where is the new BrahMos-NG plant located?
x: The Philippines is the first export customer, and the new BrahMos-NG plant is in the Lucknow Defence Corridor. B is wrong on both; C has the wrong customer; D has the wrong plant site.

s: Under the GE F414 engine deal, which manufacturing process remains with the United States?
x: The single-crystal blade process stays with the US, which limits technology transfer and keeps India dependent.

s: How many Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines does India's P-75 programme comprise?
x: P-75 comprises six Kalvari-class submarines; the last, INS Vaghsheer, was delivered in 2025.

s: How many Rafale-M jets for the Navy did India contract in April 2025?
x: 26 Rafale-M (Navy, 2025); 36 Rafale (IAF, 2016); 114 MRFA (AoN 2026).

s: Under the ₹1,943 crore lease of August 2026, India leased how many MQ-9B Sea Guardian drones for 30 months?
x: India leased 2 MQ-9B drones for 30 months for ₹1,943 crore.

s: Which company makes the MQ-9B Sea Guardian HALE drone?
x: The MQ-9B is made by US firm General Atomics.

s: What is the range of the S-400 Triumf air-defence system used in Operation Sindoor?
x: The Russian S-400 has a range of 400 km.

s: How many CQB carbines were ordered from Bharat Forge and PLR?
x: 4.25 lakh CQB carbines were ordered in a ₹4,666 crore package.

s: In February 2026, the DAC gave AoN for how many more P-8I maritime patrol aircraft?
x: The DAC cleared 6 more P-8I aircraft (US) in February 2026.

s: On which system is India's Mission Sudarshan Chakra multi-layer defence shield modelled?
x: Mission Sudarshan Chakra is modelled on Israel's Iron Dome; the S-400 called 'Sudarshan Chakra' is Russian.

s: Which was the last of the six Kalvari-class (Scorpene) submarines, commissioned in 2025?
x: INS Vaghsheer (2025) was the sixth and last P-75 Kalvari-class submarine built at MDL, Mumbai.

s: For how many Rafale jets under the MRFA did the DAC give Acceptance of Necessity on 12 February 2026?
x: The DAC gave AoN for 114 Rafale (MRFA); the IAF has 36 (2016 deal) and the Navy ordered 26 Rafale-M (2025).

s: A firm of which country got the January 2026 contract for heavyweight torpedoes for India's Kalvari-class submarines?
x: Italy's WASS got the January 2026 heavyweight torpedo contract for the Kalvari submarines.

s: From which country is the Javelin anti-tank guided missile, for which India signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance in August 2026?
x: Javelin is a US ATGM; Tata Advanced Systems has a JV MoU for its co-production in India.

s: In which countries was the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak of 2026 reported?
x: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak was reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.

s: In September 2026, the United Kingdom went ahead with handing over the Chagos Islands to which country, a move objected to by the Maldives?
x: The UK is handing the Chagos Islands to Mauritius; the Maldives objects. Seychelles, Sri Lanka and Madagascar are not parties to this handover.

o: Pakistan's operation along the Durand Line
China's renaming of places in Arunachal Pradesh
Argentina's claim over the Falkland Islands
x: India standardised 27 place names, including Longju, Maja and Thag La, in response to China's renaming of places in Arunachal Pradesh.

s: In September 2026, Israel shut which country's Jerusalem consulate after it banned trade with illegal Israeli settlements?
x: The UK (with France and Canada) banned trade with illegal Israeli settlements, and Israel responded by shutting Britain's Jerusalem consulate.

s: Amid the 2026 West Asia crisis, India deployed which Navy escort missions?
x: India deployed the Navy escort missions Sankalp and Urja Suraksha around Hormuz; it did not join the US–Israel attacks on Iran.

s: Who was sworn in as Prime Minister of Bangladesh on 17 February 2026?
x: Tarique Rahman became PM after the BNP's landslide in the 12 February 2026 election.

s: Which party's win led to Balendra (Balen) Shah being sworn in as Prime Minister of Nepal in March 2026?

x: The Falklands are disputed between the UK and Argentina.

x: East Timor was a Portuguese colony, annexed by Indonesia in 1976, and became independent in 2002.
